styles.name: 3D / WebGL immersive
styles.description: A real-time 3D scene (Three.js, React Three Fiber or Spline) is the hero and often the navigation. Type stays quiet so the object carries the story.
fitsWhen: Creative studios and agencies
Hardware, devices, wearables, cars (product you can rotate)
Games, launches, campaign microsites
Brands whose product is spatial (AR, 3D tools, architecture)
avoidWhen: B2B SaaS where the buyer needs facts fast
Audiences on low-end Android or slow networks
Pages whose main KPI is form conversion

layout.hero: Full-viewport canvas behind or around a short headline (2-6 words) and one CTA; the scene reacts to pointer and scroll.
layout.sections: Scroll-driven chapters: the camera moves through the same scene while text panels fade in; end with a plain HTML contact/CTA section.
layout.grid: Loose; text anchored to corners or a 12-col grid overlaid on the canvas.
layout.density: Very low text density; 1 idea per viewport.
layout.whitespace: Huge - the 3D scene is the whitespace.

typography.scale: Fluid clamp() sizes; H1 40-96px; weight 400-500 (measured lusion.co H1 42.75px/400, lh 1.1).

palettes.name: Lusion light (measured base)
palettes.note: bg, surface, primary blue and pill button #2B2E3A measured on lusion.co

signature.shadows: Very soft double shadow: rgba(0,0,0,.04) 0 6px 10px, rgba(0,0,0,.04) 0 2px 4px (measured lusion.co)
signature.textures: Film grain or noise in post-processing; bloom; chromatic aberration used sparingly
signature.imagery: Custom 3D models (GLB/GLTF), physically based materials, HDRI lighting, fluid or particle sims
signature.motion: Pointer parallax, scroll-scrubbed camera paths, custom cursor, page transitions via shader wipes

libraries: gsap + ScrollTrigger or motion (framer-motion) for DOM
implementation.tailwind: Keep DOM layer in Tailwind; place <Canvas> in a fixed `absolute inset-0 -z-10` wrapper; define colors as @theme tokens so shaders and CSS share values.
performance: Render a static poster image (AVIF/WebP) as the LCP element; mount the Canvas after first paint (dynamic import, requestIdleCallback).
Budget: < 250 KB JS for the 3D chunk, < 2 MB total 3D assets, Draco/Meshopt geometry, KTX2 textures.
Clamp DPR to [1, 1.5] and use PerformanceMonitor to lower quality; frameloop='demand' when the scene is static.
Pause rendering when the canvas is off-screen (IntersectionObserver) or the tab is hidden.
accessibility: prefers-reduced-motion: freeze the camera, disable auto-rotation and scroll-scrubbing, show the poster.
All content and CTAs must exist as real HTML, not text drawn in WebGL.
Provide a mobile fallback (poster or short muted loop video) under ~768px or when WebGL2 is missing.
Custom cursors must not hide the system cursor on focusable elements; keep visible focus rings.

failureModes: Default Spline blob or glossy torus that has nothing to do with the product
Loader screen with a percentage counter before any content (kills LCP and bounce rate)
Scroll hijacking that breaks trackpad momentum and keyboard navigation
Heavy bloom and purple-cyan lighting (reads as stock AI render)
Headline text baked into the 3D scene, unreadable and not indexable

references.note: 3D rotating books on an editorial page (2 canvases)

styles.name: Minimal SaaS / "Linear style" dark product
styles.description: Near-black canvas, one tight grotesk, product screenshots as hero art, and a restrained accent. Precision and speed are the message.
fitsWhen: Developer tools, productivity SaaS, AI tooling
Products with a polished UI worth showing
Technical buyers who dislike marketing fluff
avoidWhen: Products without a strong UI to screenshot
Audiences reading long text (dark mode long-form tires eyes)
When every competitor already looks like this (check the category first)

layout.hero: Left-aligned or centered H1 (2 lines), one-line subhead, primary + ghost CTA, then a large product screenshot/video that bleeds off the bottom of the viewport.
layout.sections: Logo strip, 3-5 feature chapters each with a large UI crop, changelog/speed proof, testimonials, pricing link, final CTA.
layout.grid: 12-col, 1200-1280px max width; features alternate full-width UI and 2-3 column detail grids.
layout.density: Medium-low; lots of small 13-15px secondary text.

pairings.mono: Berkeley Mono (commercial) -> JetBrains Mono / Geist Mono

pairings.note: Or swap to Hanken Grotesk / Onest to avoid the Inter-everywhere AI tell

typography.scale: H1 56-72px, H2 40-48px, body 15-16px; tight negative tracking on display (-0.02 to -0.06em); line-height 1.0-1.1 on headings.

palettes.name: Linear (measured)
palettes.note: bg, surface, ink, muted and primary measured on linear.app. Tertiary text #62666D measured there reaches only 3.45:1 - do not use for body.

palettes.name: Vercel light (measured)
palettes.note: bg, ink, muted, border and link blue oklch(0.5761 0.2508 258.23)=#006BFF measured on vercel.com

signature.radius: 6-12px on cards/buttons, pill for small nav CTAs (Linear: 9999px x76, 8px x32; Vercel: 6px)
signature.borders: 1px hairlines at 6-10% white (rgba(255,255,255,.08) measured on Linear)
signature.shadows: Nearly none; depth from lighter surfaces and inner highlights
signature.textures: Subtle radial glow or noise behind the hero screenshot; grid/dot patterns at 3-5% opacity
signature.imagery: Real product UI, often angled or cropped; no stock photos
signature.motion: Short (150-250ms) fades and masks; screenshots that assemble on scroll; keyboard-shortcut hints

implementation.tailwind: Define --color-bg, --color-surface, --color-line, --color-ink, --color-muted in @theme; use `text-balance` on H1; `tracking-[-0.022em]` utilities for display; use `border-white/8` style alpha borders.
performance: Serve hero screenshot as AVIF with explicit width/height; it is the LCP image - preload it and give it fetchpriority=high
Replace autoplay videos with poster + play-on-view
Subset variable fonts; one family + one mono
accessibility: Muted grey text on near-black must still hit 4.5:1 (Linear's #8A8F98 does at 6.1:1; its #62666D does not)
Do not rely on subtle 8% borders to convey state
Honor prefers-reduced-motion for scroll reveals
Offer a light theme or respect prefers-color-scheme for long reading

failureModes: Indigo/purple accent + Inter + centered hero + badge above H1 = the canonical AI-generated SaaS look
Glowing purple radial blob behind the hero
Three identical icon-on-top feature cards
Fake UI mockups made of grey rectangles instead of the real product
Low-contrast grey body text (below 4.5:1) chasing an 'elegant' look

styles.name: Editorial / serif-led magazine
styles.description: Reads like a well-set magazine or book: a serif carries headlines and often body, with columns, drop caps, captions and pull quotes. Authority through typography.
fitsWhen: AI labs, research orgs, think tanks, publishers
Newsletters, media, long-form content products
Premium consumer brands with a story
Founders or agencies selling judgment and taste

layout.hero: Large serif headline (often a full sentence), short standfirst, byline/date-like metadata, a single understated CTA; sometimes an illustration or photo with a caption.
layout.sections: Essay-like sections with numbered headings, pull quotes, footnotes/sidenotes, a table of contents, and an index-like footer.
layout.grid: Asymmetric editorial grid: narrow text column (60-70ch) with wide margins for notes and images.
layout.whitespace: Generous margins; tight leading in headlines.

pairings.display: Anthropic Sans 700 (commercial) + Anthropic Serif body (measured anthropic.com, body 20px)
Ivar Display / Ivar Text (commercial, measured press.stripe.com, P 25px lh 1.5)
pairings.freeSubstitute: Fraunces (opsz axis) or Newsreader for both

pairings.ui: IBM Plex Sans / Instrument Sans for labels

typography.scale: Ratio 1.333-1.5; body 18-21px with line-height 1.5-1.6; max 65ch; headlines with small negative tracking; use real italics and old-style numerals.

palettes.name: Paper (measured anthropic.com)
palettes.note: bg, surface, ink and clay accent measured on anthropic.com. Its muted #87867F reaches only 3.47:1 on the paper bg, so this palette darkens muted to #6B6A63. Clay #D97757 is decorative (3.1:1).

palettes.name: Night press (measured press.stripe.com)
palettes.note: bg #1D1A15, ink #E2CAB0, yellow #FFD943 and olive #C1B676 measured on press.stripe.com

signature.borders: Hairline rules between sections, column rules
signature.iconography: Few icons; typographic markers (numbers, dingbats, arrows)

implementation.tailwind: Use `font-feature-settings` for 'onum','liga'; `max-w-[65ch]`; `text-pretty` on paragraphs; `hyphens-auto` for narrow columns.
performance: Serif variable fonts are heavy - subset to Latin, preload only the display weight
Use font-display: swap with size-adjust fallback metrics to avoid layout shift
accessibility: Body 18px+, line-height >= 1.5
Warm grey muted text often fails contrast - check it
Keep links underlined in body text

failureModes: Playfair Display + Montserrat default pairing (overused template look)
A single italic serif word inside a sans headline as 'accent' - listed as an AI tell
Serif used only in the hero while everything else is generic SaaS
Justified text without hyphenation (rivers)
Faux-vintage ornaments without editorial content to back them

styles.name: Bento grid
styles.description: Features are packed into a mosaic of rounded tiles of different sizes, each a mini-poster with one stat, visual, or interaction.
fitsWhen: Products with many features of similar weight
Hardware spec summaries (Apple style)
Portfolios and link-in-bio pages
Feature overview sections inside other styles
avoidWhen: When each tile would contain the same icon+heading+2 lines

layout.hero: Usually a conventional hero; the bento appears right below as the feature overview, or the whole hero is one large tile inside the grid.
layout.sections: 1-3 bento clusters (6-9 tiles each), each cluster with a section heading; tiles mix screenshots, big numbers, mini-animations, quotes.
layout.grid: CSS grid with 4-6 columns on desktop; tiles span 1-3 columns and 1-2 rows; collapses to 1-2 columns on mobile.
layout.whitespace: Consistent 12-24px gutters; generous padding inside tiles (24-40px).

pairings.display: GT Walsheim Medium (commercial, measured framer.com H1 54px/500 ls -0.04em)

typography.scale: Tile headings 20-28px, tile stats 48-96px; body 15-17px; keep one type family per page.

palettes.name: Framer dark (measured)
palettes.note: bg #000, tile surface #242424, muted #999999 and blue #0099FF measured on framer.com. White on #0099FF is only 3.0:1, so use black button text or a darker blue.

signature.radius: 16-28px tiles (framer.com: 8px x230, 15px x71, 20px x24); nested radius = outer - padding
signature.shadows: None or very soft; tiles separated by surface color
signature.iconography: Large illustrative icons or real UI crops, not generic line icons
signature.motion: Tile hover lift, looping micro-animations inside tiles, staggered reveal

implementation.tailwind: `grid grid-cols-2 md:grid-cols-6 auto-rows-[minmax(180px,auto)] gap-4`; tiles use `md:col-span-2 md:row-span-2`; use `grid-flow-dense` carefully (it reorders visually but not for screen readers).
performance: Lazy-load tile videos; pause off-screen loops
Avoid a canvas per tile
accessibility: Keep DOM order = reading order; don't let grid-flow-dense scramble the logical order
Each tile needs a real heading
Tiles that are links need one clear link target, not nested links

failureModes: Every tile identical: icon, heading, two lines (just a card grid)
Random spans that don't reflect importance
Too many tiles (>12) in one cluster - becomes a wall
Mobile collapse to one tall column of 12 tiles with no hierarchy

styles.name: Neo-brutalism / brutalist
styles.description: Thick black outlines, hard offset shadows, flat saturated fills and blunt type. It looks deliberately raw but is structured and usable.
fitsWhen: Creator tools, indie SaaS, marketplaces (Gumroad)
Gen Z consumer apps, hackathons, communities
Brands positioning against polished corporate competitors
avoidWhen: Audiences that equate polish with trust

layout.hero: Huge headline (80-120px), sticker-like badges, a chunky bordered CTA with hard shadow; sometimes a marquee ticker.
layout.sections: Bordered blocks with alternating flat color backgrounds, big numbers, testimonial 'cards' tilted a few degrees, FAQ as bordered accordions.
layout.grid: Visible grid; blocks separated by 2-4px black borders instead of whitespace.
layout.whitespace: Less whitespace; borders do the separation.

typography.scale: Big jumps (ratio 1.5-1.618); display 72-120px; body 18px; uppercase labels with letter-spacing.

palettes.name: Gumroad (measured)
palettes.note: bg #F4F4F0, pink #FF90E8, yellow #FFC900 measured on gumroad.com (also #F1F333, #DC341E). Pink is a fill - text on it must be black (10.4:1); white would be 2.0:1.

palettes.name: neobrutalism.dev (measured)
palettes.note: main bg, blue #5294FF and yellow #FACC00 measured; buttons have 2px #000 border, 5px radius and box-shadow 4px 4px 0 0 #000

signature.radius: 0-8px, or full pills (gumroad.com uses pills x129)
signature.shadows: Hard offset, no blur: 4px 4px 0 0 #000 (measured neobrutalism.dev); hover translates the element into its shadow
signature.textures: Flat fills; occasional halftone or sticker graphics
signature.iconography: Chunky filled icons, emoji-like stickers, hand-drawn doodles
signature.imagery: Cut-out photos with outlines, flat illustrations
signature.motion: Snappy (100-150ms) press-in on click, marquees, wiggle on hover

implementation.tailwind: Tokens: `--shadow-brutal: 4px 4px 0 0 var(--color-ink)`; button: `border-2 border-ink shadow-brutal active:translate-x-1 active:translate-y-1 active:shadow-none`.
performance: Cheap to render; keep marquees CSS-only (transform) and pause offscreen
accessibility: Saturated fills + white text often fail - use black text on pastels
Marquees need pause control and must stop under prefers-reduced-motion
Don't let tilted cards break reading or focus order

failureModes: Random clashing colors with no system (brutal ≠ arbitrary)
Offset shadows in different directions/lengths across components
White text on bright pink/yellow fills
Applying the style to a serious enterprise product where it erodes trust

styles.name: Glassmorphism / aurora gradient mesh
styles.description: Soft, blurred color fields (mesh or aurora gradients) sit behind translucent frosted panels. Depth comes from light and blur instead of borders.
fitsWhen: Fintech and payments (Stripe mesh), AI consumer apps, wellness tech
OS/platform-adjacent products (Apple Liquid Glass era)
Launch pages where a mood matters more than density
avoidWhen: Text-heavy pages (text on blur loses contrast)
Low-end devices (backdrop-filter costs 15-30% FPS in field reports)
When the gradient is the only idea

layout.hero: Animated gradient mesh canvas or CSS blobs behind a crisp H1; product UI in a frosted card floating above.
layout.sections: White or dark neutral sections punctuated by gradient 'moments'; frosted nav bar; feature cards with subtle transparency.

pairings.freeSubstitute: Onest / Hanken Grotesk to avoid Inter default

typography.scale: Light display weights (300-400) read elegant over color; H1 48-72px; body 16-18px.

palettes.name: Stripe mesh light (measured)
palettes.note: ink #061B31, muted #50617A and primary #533AFD measured on stripe.com (canvas gradient present). Suggested mesh stops: #A960EE, #FF333D, #90E0FF, #FFCB57 (Stripe's public gradient, not measured).

palettes.name: Aurora night
palettes.note: Glow stops: #7CF5C8, #5B8CFF, #FF7AB6 at 30-50% opacity over bg; panels rgba(255,255,255,0.05-0.08) with 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.12) border (Raycast measured rgba(255,255,255,.05) x104)

signature.shadows: Layered keycap/inset shadows (Raycast: rgba(0,0,0,.4) 0 1.5px .5px 2.5px, #000 0 0 .5px 1px, rgba(0,0,0,.25) 0 2px 1px 1px inset)
signature.textures: Noise overlay (2-4%) to prevent gradient banding
signature.imagery: Gradient meshes, light leaks, 3D glass objects
signature.motion: Slowly drifting gradients (20-40s loops), cursor-following glow

libraries: Stripe-style minigl gradient (WebGL) or CSS radial-gradient blobs
implementation.tailwind: `backdrop-blur-xl bg-white/5 border border-white/10`; limit blur to nav/modals/1-2 hero panels (Raycast measured 21 blurred elements, Rolex 45 - high).
performance: backdrop-filter is expensive on scroll; don't stack blurred layers
Render gradient as CSS or a single small canvas; pause when hidden
Add noise via a tiny tiled PNG, not an SVG filter on a large area
accessibility: Check contrast on the worst point of the gradient, not the average
Provide solid fallback: @supports not (backdrop-filter) -> opaque surface
prefers-reduced-transparency (Safari/Chromium flag) -> opaque panels; prefers-reduced-motion -> static gradient

failureModes: Purple-to-blue/cyan gradient behind a centered Inter headline (the #1 AI tell)
Glass cards with neon glow on everything
Banding in gradients (no dithering/noise)
Text directly on the brightest part of the mesh

styles.name: Swiss / International typographic grid
styles.description: Objective, grid-driven layouts with a neo-grotesk, strong alignment, flush-left text and one signal color. Order is the aesthetic.
fitsWhen: Design studios, architecture, typefoundries, museums, events
Hardware and industrial design (teenage.engineering)
Research tools and knowledge products (Are.na)
avoidWhen: Teams without discipline to keep the grid (it breaks visibly)

layout.hero: Oversized flush-left headline or wordmark set on the grid, small metadata columns (date, location, index numbers), no decorative imagery; or a single large photo cropped to grid.
layout.sections: Numbered sections, tables and lists, index pages, captions in small type.
layout.grid: Strict 12-col (or 6/8) with visible alignment; sometimes grid lines drawn.
layout.density: Varies - sparse posters or dense index tables.

pairings.mono: IBM Plex Mono for index numbers

typography.scale: Few sizes with big contrast (e.g. 12/16/24/96); flush-left, ragged-right; tight headline leading (0.9-1.0).

palettes.name: Are.na grey (measured)
palettes.note: ink #333333, muted #696969, navy button #00075F and #DEDEDE measured on are.na (bg there is #FFFFFF with #F7F7F7 surfaces)

signature.imagery: Documentary photography, product on seamless, grid-cropped
signature.motion: Minimal; instant state changes, hover underlines

implementation.tailwind: `grid grid-cols-12 gap-x-4`; use `col-start-*` to place text off-center; debug overlay with a `bg-[repeating-linear-gradient]` grid toggle.
performance: Very light; images are the only weight
accessibility: Tiny metadata type (11-12px) must still pass contrast; keep body >=16px
Red accents fail on some backgrounds - check

failureModes: Helvetica + red without a real grid (pastiche)
All text the same size - no hierarchy
Centered layouts (breaks the idiom)

styles.name: Playful / illustrated / colorful
styles.description: Bright color, rounded forms, mascots or custom illustration, and bouncy micro-interactions. The product feels friendly before you read a word.
fitsWhen: Consumer apps, education, kids/family, games
SMB tools that want to feel human (Mailchimp, Notion illustrations)
Community products
avoidWhen: When no budget for original illustration (stock illustration looks cheap)

layout.hero: Mascot or illustration beside a short, bold headline and one big rounded CTA.
layout.sections: Alternating illustration/text rows, colored section bands, stats with friendly icons, app store badges.

pairings.display: Feather Bold / DIN Next Rounded (commercial, measured duolingo.com)

typography.scale: Rounded, heavy display (700-900); body 17-18px at weight 500 (measured duolingo P 17px/500).

palettes.name: Duolingo (measured)
palettes.note: ink #3C3C3C, muted #777777, green #58CC02, blue #1CB0F6, surface #DDF4FF measured. Duolingo sets white uppercase text on #58CC02: 2.09:1, a WCAG fail even for large text. This palette uses dark text #0B2A00 instead. Measured muted #777777 is 4.48:1 on white (just under AA), so muted is darkened to #6F6F6F.

signature.shadows: Solid bottom 'press' border (Duolingo buttons: 4px bottom border, 12px radius, 15px/700 uppercase, ls 0.8px - measured)
signature.motion: Springy (overshoot) transitions, character reactions, Rive state machines

implementation.tailwind: Tokens for 4-6 brand colors; `rounded-2xl`; custom `shadow-[0_4px_0_0_var(--color-primary-dark)]` press effect.
performance: Rive files are small and GPU-rendered; prefer over large Lottie JSON
Lazy-load below-fold animations
accessibility: Bright brand greens/blues/oranges almost always fail with white text - use dark text or darken the fill
Mascot animations: respect prefers-reduced-motion; add alt text

failureModes: Generic 'corporate Memphis' flat people with purple skin
Stock illustration packs mixed in different styles
Too many colors with no hierarchy
White text on saturated brand color

styles.name: Dense technical / developer docs-like
styles.description: Monospace or near-mono type, flat surfaces, dense information, code blocks and tables above the fold. It signals 'built by engineers for engineers'.
fitsWhen: Databases, infra, APIs, CLIs, open-source projects
Technical buyers who evaluate by docs
Brands positioning against glossy SaaS (the 'anti-grid' reaction noted in 2026)

layout.hero: Small headline (can be the same size as body - PlanetScale sets H1 at 16px/700), a one-paragraph pitch, install command or code block, and 1-2 flat CTAs.
layout.sections: Benchmarks tables, code samples with tabs, changelog, customer quotes as plain text, pricing table with numbers.
layout.grid: Single column 70-90ch or docs-like sidebar + content.

pairings.display: ui-monospace / SF Mono (system, measured planetscale.com everything at 16px)

typography.scale: Compressed scale (ratio 1.125-1.2) or flat; hierarchy via weight, color and rules, not size.

palettes.name: PlanetScale (measured)
palettes.note: bg #FAFAFA, text #414141, black button #111111, orange oklch(0.6622 0.2377 39.25)~#FF4400 and link oklch(0.5358 0.191 252.41)~#006BD7 measured. PlanetScale puts white text on the orange: ~3.4:1, fails AA for 16px text; this palette uses black.

signature.imagery: Code, terminal output, architecture diagrams, charts
signature.motion: Typing effect for commands (short), copy-button feedback

libraries: fumadocs / nextra patterns for docs-like layout
performance: Very light; highlight code at build time, not client-side
accessibility: All-monospace body reduces reading speed - keep paragraphs short
Copy buttons need aria-live feedback
Tables need <th scope>

failureModes: Fake terminal hero with made-up commands
Matrix-green on black cliché
Density without hierarchy - everything bold
Tiny 12-13px mono body text

styles.name: Retro / Y2K / pixel / retro-OS
styles.description: Nostalgic computing: pixel fonts, desktop windows, chrome gradients, stickers and CRT textures. In 2025-26 the 'website as a desktop OS' variant became mainstream (PostHog).
fitsWhen: Music, culture, fashion drops, creator communities
Developer brands with humor (PostHog)
Games and indie apps
avoidWhen: Accessibility-critical public services (pixel fonts hurt legibility)
When the joke hides the product

layout.hero: A fake desktop with draggable windows, icons and a menu bar; or a Y2K chrome logo on a starfield/gradient.
layout.sections: Content inside window chrome; taskbar/dock navigation; guestbook/marquee sections.
layout.grid: Free-form, overlapping windows (desktop) - with a normal stacked layout on mobile.

typography.scale: Pixel fonts at integer multiples of their design size (8/16/24/32px) to stay crisp; body in a readable font.

palettes.name: Poolsuite (measured)
palettes.note: bg #F6D5D5, window #F9F0E9, #FAF4C6 and #000 measured on poolsuite.net

palettes.name: PostHog retro OS (measured)
palettes.note: bg #EEEFE9, surface #FDFDF8, ink #111827, body #374151, orange #EB9D2A with #111111 text and 1.5px #B17816 border, hard bottom shadow rgb(210,211,204) 0 2.5px 0 - measured on posthog.com

signature.shadows: Hard drop shadows, bevel/inset (Win95), large soft window shadow (poolsuite: rgba(0,0,0,.3) 0 50px 80px -50px)
signature.imagery: Pixel art, low-poly 3D, stickers, lo-fi photos

implementation.tailwind: Disable font smoothing for pixel fonts (`[-webkit-font-smoothing:none]`), `image-rendering: pixelated` on sprites.
performance: Desktop metaphors can load many apps at once - lazy-load window contents
accessibility: Draggable windows need keyboard alternatives and a linear mobile layout
Never set body copy in pixel fonts
Blinking/marquee must stop under prefers-reduced-motion (WCAG 2.2.2)

failureModes: Pixel font for paragraphs
Nostalgia without a concept (random 90s stickers)
Desktop metaphor that hides the CTA
Mobile shows the desktop scaled down

styles.name: Luxury / premium dark
styles.description: Dark, restrained, image-led pages with thin serifs or wide caps, lots of air and very slow motion. Scarcity and craft over information.
fitsWhen: Watches, jewelry, fashion, hotels, cars, spirits
Premium services (private banking, architecture)
High-end B2C launches
avoidWhen: Dense catalogs where filters matter more than mood

layout.hero: Full-bleed photography or video, small centered wordmark, one line of caps or thin serif, discreet 'Discover' link.
layout.sections: Alternating full-bleed images and short copy blocks; product detail with macro shots; appointment/boutique CTA.

pairings.display: Helvetica Now Text 700 (commercial, measured rolex.com H2 90.7px/700 lh 0.95 over video)

typography.scale: Big contrast between very large display and small, widely tracked labels (11-13px caps, 0.12-0.25em).

palettes.name: Noir and gold
palettes.note: Burgundy secondary is decorative only on this bg

palettes.name: Crown green (Rolex measured accent)
palettes.note: green #127749 and ink #212121 measured on rolex.com; Rolex hero CTA is rgba(118,118,118,.3) glass pill with white 16px/700 text over video

signature.imagery: Professional macro photography, slow cinematic video
signature.motion: Slow (600-1200ms) eased fades, parallax on imagery

libraries: next/image or unpic for responsive images
implementation.tailwind: Tokens for gold/ink; `tracking-[0.2em] uppercase text-xs` labels; `aspect-[4/5]` product imagery.
performance: Hero video: poster is the LCP; <2 MB muted H.264/AV1 loop; no autoplay on mobile data-saver
AVIF images with srcset
accessibility: Gold on black and thin weights often fail - check at actual weight
Text over video needs a scrim (gradient overlay) for contrast
Pause control for background video (WCAG 2.2.2)

failureModes: Gold gradient text and fake metallic effects
Stock luxury photos (champagne, marble)
Thin 200-weight grey body text
Script fonts

styles.name: Organic / warm natural
styles.description: Cream and earth tones, soft serif or humanist sans, natural photography and textures. Calm, sensory and human.
fitsWhen: Skincare, food, wellness, hospitality, sustainability
Healthcare and therapy practices
AI or tech brands wanting to feel human (Anthropic's warm paper palette)

layout.hero: Large natural photograph or still life, short headline, understated text link CTA; sometimes a split layout (text left, image right).
layout.sections: Ingredient/story sections, image-led product rows, long-form journal content, store locator.

typography.scale: Modest sizes, regular weights; relaxed line-height (1.4-1.6).

palettes.name: Aesop cream (measured)
palettes.note: bg #FFFEF2, ink #333333, grey #666666 button, surface #F6F5E8 measured on aesop.com

signature.textures: Paper, linen, grain, botanical line drawings
signature.imagery: Natural-light photography, raw materials, hands, plants

implementation.tailwind: Warm neutral scale in @theme (not Tailwind's cool stone/zinc defaults).
performance: Photography is the weight - AVIF, responsive sizes, lazy below fold
accessibility: Aesop sets body at 12-14px; keep >=16px
Warm grey on cream: check muted text (#666 on #FFFEF2 = 5.66:1 passes)

failureModes: Beige everything with no contrast or accent
Stock leaves and generic 'wellness' photos
Blob shapes with no purpose
Tiny body text for elegance

styles.name: Kinetic typography / motion-heavy
styles.description: Type is the image: headlines split, scale, scroll horizontally, morph weight or react to the cursor. Usually monochrome so motion carries the brand.
fitsWhen: Agencies, studios, portfolios, events and festivals
Brand launches and campaigns
Music and fashion
avoidWhen: Content read by screen-reader-heavy audiences unless done carefully

layout.hero: One oversized word or line (10-20vw) animated on load; minimal nav; scroll cue.
layout.sections: Pinned sections with text scrubbed by scroll, horizontal-scroll project rows, marquee client lists, big footer wordmark.
layout.grid: Edge-to-edge; type often bleeds past the viewport.

pairings.freeSubstitute: Big Shoulders Display or Anton + Inter Tight

pairings.display: Roboto Flex / Recursive (variable axes to animate)

palettes.name: Locomotive mono (measured)
palettes.note: locomotive.ca uses only 4 distinct colors: #000, #FFF and blue #312DFB (measured). Surface flips to black sections with white text.

signature.imagery: Project videos revealed by text masks
signature.motion: Split-text reveals, scroll-scrubbed scale, horizontal scroll, variable-font weight animation, magnetic cursor

implementation.tailwind: Fluid type via `text-[clamp(3rem,12vw,14rem)] leading-[0.85] tracking-tight`; `overflow-hidden` wrappers for line masks.
performance: Animate transform/opacity only; avoid animating font-size/layout
Split text only above-the-fold headline; don't split long paragraphs
accessibility: Keep the unsplit text for screen readers (aria-label on parent, aria-hidden on split spans)
prefers-reduced-motion: show final state immediately
Don't hijack scroll speed; don't pin for more than ~1-2 viewports
Motion over 5s needs pause (WCAG 2.2.2)

failureModes: Letter-by-letter reveals on every heading (slow and tiring)
Scroll-jacking and long pinned sections
Text that is illegible mid-animation when a user lands via anchor link
Motion without content - agency reel with no CTA

styles.name: Cinematic full-bleed photo/video hero
styles.description: A full-viewport photo or video with oversized plain sans type laid on top, then calm sections. Listed as a 2026 trend ('cinematic heroes').
fitsWhen: Travel, hospitality, outdoor, automotive, events
Consumer hardware with great footage
Brands with a strong photo library
avoidWhen: No original footage (stock video looks cheap)
Products that need a UI screenshot to explain

layout.hero: 100svh media with scrim, H1 bottom-left, one CTA; nav transparent over the media.
layout.sections: Short copy + image pairs, gallery, booking/CTA band.

pairings.note: overused in AI output - use only with a real editorial reason

palettes.name: Night overlay
palettes.note: Always put a 40-60% black gradient scrim under hero text

performance: Poster image is LCP; preload it; video preload='none' on mobile
Serve 720p/1080p variants
accessibility: Pause button for background video
Scrim for text contrast
Captions if the video carries meaning

failureModes: Stock drone footage
Text over busy imagery without scrim
Autoplay video with sound

references.note: trend article listing cinematic hero examples

styles.name: Maximalist / collage / anti-design
styles.description: Dense, layered compositions: cut-out photos, scribbles, stickers, clashing type and torn paper. Energy and personality over order.
fitsWhen: Beverage and fashion brands (Liquid Death-style)
Festivals, zines, music
Brands that want to stand out in a sea of minimal SaaS

layout.hero: Collage of overlapping elements with a huge headline and sticker CTA.
layout.sections: Layered scrapbook panels, rotated elements, mixed type.
layout.grid: Broken or overlapping; still an underlying grid for text blocks.

pairings.accent: Caveat or Permanent Marker for scribbles

implementation.tailwind: Absolute-positioned layers inside a relative container; `rotate-[-3deg]` utilities.
performance: Many large PNG cutouts - use WebP/AVIF with alpha, sprite small stickers
accessibility: Keep a clean reading layer for real text
Decorative images aria-hidden

failureModes: Chaos with no focal point or CTA
Illegible text over collage
Clip-art stickers

references.note: lists maximalism and collage as 2026 trends

fundamentals.check: Use a consistent modular type scale (ratio 1.2-1.333 for product/SaaS, 1.414-1.618 for expressive/editorial). Measured: Linear 15/48/64, Vercel 24/56/64, Gumroad 18/48/96.
fundamentals.pass: <= 6-7 distinct font sizes on the page; each maps to a role

fundamentals.check: Large display type gets negative tracking (-0.01 to -0.04em; Vercel goes to -0.06em); small caps labels get positive tracking (+0.05 to +0.2em). Body stays at 0.
Body line-height 1.4-1.6; headings 0.9-1.2 (tighter as size grows).
fundamentals.pass: No 1.5 line-height on 64px headings; no 1.2 on body

fundamentals.check: One dominant element per viewport (usually H1 or hero visual); clear H1 > H2 > body steps via size, weight and color.
fundamentals.pass: Squint test: the eye lands on H1, then CTA, then supporting visual

fundamentals.check: Spacing from a 4px or 8px base with a limited set of steps (e.g. 4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96,128); section padding consistent.
fundamentals.pass: No arbitrary values like 13px/37px; same gap for same relationship

fundamentals.check: WCAG 2.2 AA: 4.5:1 body text, 3:1 large text (>=24px or >=18.66px bold) and UI components/focus indicators. Check muted text and button text on brand color - measured failures: Duolingo white-on-green 2.09:1, PlanetScale white-on-orange ~3.4:1, Anthropic muted 3.47:1, Linear tertiary 3.45:1.
fundamentals.pass: All text meets AA at its actual size and weight

fundamentals.check: One primary CTA per view with a verb-led label; secondary CTA visually weaker (ghost/link). Primary CTA visible without scrolling.
fundamentals.pass: Exactly one filled primary button above the fold

fundamentals.check: Above the fold states what it is, for whom, and why (headline + subhead), shows the product or proof, and holds the primary CTA. NN/g: 57% of viewing time is above the fold, 74% in the first two screenfuls.
fundamentals.pass: A stranger can say what the product does after 5 seconds

fundamentals.check: Neutral scale + 1 primary accent + at most 1-2 secondary accents, all as tokens. Measured distinct color counts (text+bg union): locomotive 4, gumroad 9, planetscale 11, vercel 15, anthropic 15, linear 50, framer 53.
fundamentals.pass: Accent used for action/emphasis only; no ad-hoc hex values

fundamentals.check: Same radius family, shadow family, icon style and button styles across the page; nested radius = outer radius - padding.
fundamentals.pass: <= 3 radius values, <= 2 shadow styles, one icon set

fundamentals.check: Avoid the generic AI look: Inter-only + indigo/purple gradient + centered hero + badge above H1 + three identical icon cards + stat row + colored left-border cards + 'Build faster. Ship smarter.' copy. Also overused as 'safe alternatives': Space Grotesk, Instrument Serif, Geist, italic serif accent word.
fundamentals.pass: At least 2 deliberate, product-specific choices (type, color, layout, imagery) that a template would not make

fundamentals.check: Use real product screenshots, real numbers, named customers; no lorem ipsum, no grey-box fake UI, no stock people.
fundamentals.pass: Every visual could only belong to this product

fundamentals.check: Mobile-first: 16px+ body, 44x44px tap targets (WCAG 2.5.8 min 24x24), no horizontal scroll, hero fits 375x667 with CTA visible, heavy effects replaced with static fallbacks.
Core Web Vitals: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1. Hero media: poster/static image is the LCP element; WebGL and video are progressive enhancement.
fundamentals.pass: Lighthouse mobile performance >= 85 on the built page

fundamentals.check: Respect prefers-reduced-motion; auto-moving content > 5s needs pause (WCAG 2.2.2); no scroll-jacking; animate transform/opacity only.
fundamentals.pass: Page is fully usable with reduced motion on

fundamentals.check: Visible focus rings, semantic landmarks, one H1, headings in order, alt text, real buttons/links.
